title: COPY of a member no library holds, while a program member of that name exists
realism: Linkage copybooks are often named after their program (ORDPRICE, SHPRATE) and are the first thing lost in an export. A resolver that falls back to any member of that name finds the program source.
shapes: ORDMAIN: COPY ORDPRICE; ORDPRICE.cbl is a program, no copy library holds ORDPRICE
SHPINQ: COPY SHPRATE; SHPRATE.cbl is a program
asserts: The COPY is a fact with resolves_to null and a gap: the compiler searches the SYSLIB libraries only, and a program source member is in none of them. No import edge may point at the program member.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If no library name is specified in the COPY statement, the concatenation of datasets allocated to the SYSLIB ddname is searched.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The effect of processing a COPY statement is that the library text associated with text-name is copied into the compilation unit, logically replacing the entire COPY statement, beginning with the word COPY and ending with the period, inclusive.
